headline: I Joined an International Defence Pact WhatsApp Group Thinking It Was a Neighborhood Watch Initiative
body:
I honestly thought I was joining a group to discuss pothole repairs on my street in South Delhi, but for the last three weeks, I have been receiving detailed schematics for supersonic missiles and cryptic voice notes about regional geopolitical alignment. It turns out that when my neighbor sent me the link, he had accidentally copy-pasted a secure ministerial invitation instead of the local Resident Welfare Association group. 

At first, I tried to politely inform them that they had the wrong number, but every time I sent a 'Hi, wrong group' message, I was met with rapid-fire responses in three different languages discussing naval maneuver protocols. I didn't want to seem rude or uncooperative, so I have spent the last fortnight dutifully reacting to their classified intelligence leaks with '👍' and 'Great update, keep up the hard work' emojis. 

My biggest concern isn't even the national security implication; it’s that I’m still the only person in my building who hasn't been added to the actual trash collection schedule. Last Tuesday, while I was being briefed on the logistical challenges of a multi-country military exercise, I accidentally replied with 'Is the garbage truck coming tomorrow?' The entire chat went silent for six hours, and I’m genuinely worried that if I leave now, I might be considered a defector.
caption: When you accidentally join the wrong geopolitical alliance. Have you ever been added to a group that was way above your pay grade? #Geopolitics #WrongGroup #Diplomacy #Oops (satire)
igHook: Would you stay in the group if you were getting classified military updates, or hit exit immediately?
